title: Retired Agents Now Get a 403, Not the Leader Slot | vitalii.no
description:
How a disabled-agents list on Cloudflare Workers stopped a retired automation agent from silently seizing control.

One of my automated agents, running under a default identity with no explicit id, kept waking up on its own schedule long after I'd retired it. Worse, it was occasionally winning the leader election among my agents and taking over control, running code that was already out of date everywhere else in the system.

Every agent now sends its identity in an X-Agent-Id header on every request. The Worker reads a disabled-agents list stored in KV, a simple JSON array of retired ids, and checks every incoming request against it. The leader-election logic was also patched to read that same header when none was supplied in the request body, closing the exact gap that had let the old agent claim the default identity silently.

Any request from a disabled id is now rejected outright with a 403, and the id only becomes available again if I remove it from the list by hand.
